Yes. Ciprofloxacin is a potent inhibitor of CYP1A2, and theophylline is cleared principally via CYP1A2. Inhibiting this enzyme would reduce theophylline clearance and raise its serum concentrations. Because theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range (and is monitored in practice), elevated levels risk toxicity (e.g., seizures, arrhythmias), making this a clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction. Dose reduction or alternative antibiotic is typically advised.
